_note: Sample bank so the repo runs out of the box. The production bank (content.json) stays private so players cannot read the answers.

finance.why: An IPO is when a private company first sells its shares to the public on a stock exchange.

finance.q: In a bear market, prices are generally...
finance.why: A bear market usually means prices fell 20% or more from a recent high. Bears swipe down, bulls charge up.

history.q: In which year did World War II end?
history.why: Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan in September 1945.

history.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
history.why: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon in July 1969. Buzz Aldrin followed minutes later.

science.q: Which planet has the most known moons?
science.why: Saturn passed 270 known moons after 128 new ones were confirmed in 2025, far ahead of Jupiter.

science.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
science.why: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and a third pumps it to the rest of the body.

geography.q: Which letter appears in no US state name?
geography.why: Q is the only letter missing from every US state name. J appears in New Jersey.

geography.q: Which country spans the most time zones, counting overseas territories?
geography.why: Its territories from Polynesia to Réunion give France 12 time zones.

tech.q: Which language did Brendan Eich create in about 10 days?
tech.why: Brendan Eich wrote the first JavaScript in about 10 days at Netscape in 1995.

tech.q: In which year did the first iPhone launch?
tech.why: Steve Jobs unveiled the iPhone in January 2007 and it went on sale that June.

culture.q: Which painter cut off part of his own ear?
culture.why: Vincent van Gogh cut off part of his left ear in 1888 after a quarrel with Paul Gauguin.

culture.q: Which game character first appeared under the name Jumpman?
culture.why: Mario debuted as Jumpman in Donkey Kong in 1981 and got his famous name soon after.

guess.q: How old was Warren Buffett when he bought his first stock?
guess.why: He bought three shares of Cities Service in 1942, at age 11.

guess.q: In what year was the first email sent between computers?
guess.why: Ray Tomlinson sent the first networked email on ARPANET in 1971 and picked the @ sign.

guess.q: How far is the Moon from Earth, on average?
guess.why: About 238,900 miles, roughly 30 Earths lined up side by side.

guess.q: How many people lived in New York City at the 2020 census?
guess.why: 8,804,190, more than Los Angeles and Chicago combined.

guess.q: In what year did the first website go online?
guess.why: Tim Berners-Lee put info.cern.ch online in August 1991.
26.2 miles (42.195 km), fixed in 1921 after the route of the 1908 London Olympics.

code.title: Flip it
hints: [...s] or s.split("") turns the string into an array of characters.
Arrays have .reverse(); join("") turns the result back into a string.

code.title: Add it all up
code.prompt: Return the sum of an array of numbers. An empty array sums to 0.
hints: Start a total at 0 and add each number.
reduce((total, n) => total + n, 0) does it in one line.

code.title: Vowel counter
code.prompt: Count the vowels a, e, i, o, u in any case.
hints: Lowercase the string so 'A' and 'a' count the same.
Count the characters found in "aeiou", or use a regex with match().

code.title: Palindrome check
code.prompt: Return true if the text reads the same both ways, ignoring case and spaces.
hidden: A man a plan a canal Panama
hints: Lowercase the text and remove the spaces first.
Compare the cleaned text with its reverse.

code.title: Tip calculator
code.prompt: A bill is given in cents. Return the tip in cents, rounded to the nearest cent.
hints: Multiply the bill by the percent and divide by 100.
Math.round() rounds to the nearest whole cent.

code.title: Split the bill
code.prompt: Split a bill in cents fairly: everyone pays the same, and leftover cents go to the first people. Return the shares.
hints: Math.floor(total / people) is everyone's base share.
total % people is how many people pay one extra cent.

code.label: No loops
code.desc: for and while are banned. Get creative.

code.label: One-liner
code.desc: Your whole solution must fit on a single line.

guess.label: Bullseye
guess.desc: Only close guesses score, but they score 1.5 times as much.

scam.label: Speed round
scam.desc: 6 seconds per message. Trust your gut.

scam.body: USPS: Your package is on hold because of an incomplete address. Update it within 12 hours: usps-redelivery-help.com
scam.why: USPS only texts tracking updates you asked for, and its only site is usps.com. A deadline plus a lookalike link is the classic package scam.

scam.body: Your payment failed and your membership will be cancelled today. Update your card now: netflx-account.com/update
scam.why: Read the domain: netflx is missing an i. Open the app yourself to check billing instead of using the link.

scam.body: Your verification code is 482913. Don't share this code with anyone. We'll never call to ask for it.
scam.why: You asked for it seconds ago, it has no link, and it warns you not to share it. Type it in and you're done.
scam.context: You just tapped "Send code" while logging in to your bank app.

scam.body: Thanks for calling. To verify your identity, can you confirm the last 4 digits of your card and your ZIP code?
scam.why: You started the call on a number you trust, and they ask for limited details, not your PIN, full card number or one-time code.
scam.context: You called the number printed on the back of your debit card.

myth.q: Checking your own credit score lowers it.
myth.why: Checking your own score is a soft inquiry and never affects it. Hard inquiries come from applying for credit.

myth.q: You need to carry a credit card balance to build credit.
myth.why: Paying in full every month builds the same history without paying any interest.

myth.q: Closing an old credit card can lower your credit score.
myth.why: It cuts your available credit, which raises your utilization, and can shorten the average age of your accounts.

myth.q: Your salary is part of your credit score.
myth.why: Credit scores use your borrowing history, not your income.

myth.q: You can take out the money you put into a Roth IRA at any time without tax or penalty.
myth.why: Contributions come out first and are always tax and penalty free. The earnings have stricter rules.

myth.q: Over long periods, US stocks have grown far more than savings accounts.
myth.why: US stocks have averaged roughly 10% a year over the past century before inflation, with big swings along the way.

first.why: YouTube launched in 2005; the first iPhone went on sale in 2007.

w: Isaac Newton published his laws of motion
first.why: Harvard was founded in 1636; Newton published his laws in 1687.
The Diners Club card launched in 1950; Ray Kroc opened his first McDonald's in 1955.
Alexander Bain patented an early fax in 1843, 33 years before Bell's telephone patent.
